title: Lesson 18: Guardrails II, Output Validation, Allowlists, PII Redaction, and Refusal Paths
description: Input guardrails keep an attacker from pushing the agent past its boundary. Output guardrails keep the agent from pushing bad output out the other side: validation, allowlists, PII redaction, and refusal paths.

questions.question: When you gate which actions an agent may take, why is an allowlist safer than a denylist?
options: An allowlist denies by default, so anything you did not think to list is refused.
An allowlist runs its checks faster than a denylist can at runtime.
A denylist cannot express a rule that blocks more than one value at a time.
A denylist requires the model itself to confirm every blocked action before it runs.
questions.explanation: An allowlist denies by default and fails closed on anything unnamed, while a denylist admits by default and lets through whatever you forgot to list.

questions.question: Why should output validation run its cheapest structural checks before its expensive semantic checks?
options: Semantic checks are deterministic, so they must always run last.
Cheap checks reject most bad output, so the costly pass only sees survivors.
Structural checks would corrupt the output if they ran out of order.
The model can only ever be invoked one single time for each response it produces.
questions.explanation: Running cheap structural checks first rejects most bad output at almost no cost, so the expensive semantic pass only runs on what survives.

questions.question: What is a required property of a safe refusal path when the output gate rejects a response?
options: It always retries generation until the gate finally passes.
It shows the user the exact validation error that fired.
It returns a neutral message and logs the detailed reason separately.
It forwards the rejected output straight to the downstream system regardless.
questions.explanation: A safe refusal returns a neutral message with no echo of the rejected content and logs the detailed reason out of band, so it neither leaks data nor helps an attacker.
